comments.body:
Merging a DUPLICATE I filed into this one. I created c5ca-b32b-5e9e-4053 (rebellious-tyrannous-kitty) for the same defect 14 seconds after this ticket existed, because I did not search before filing. This ticket is authoritative -- it was first and it already carries file_impact and the discovered_from link. c5ca is being closed as a duplicate.

Carrying over the two acceptance criteria from mine that may not be in yours, since they are the ones that stop a concurrency fix from being self-satisfying:

DEFECT-SEEDED PROOF. Restoring the unlocked fast path must make the reproduction test fail again --
demonstrate by mutation, then revert. This matters more than usual here: a race test that passes
because the race did not happen to fire is indistinguishable from one that passes because the race is
fixed. The mutation is what tells them apart.

REPRODUCTION MUST BE DETERMINISTIC, NOT STATISTICAL. AC1 should force the interleaving -- hold the
lock while a bundle is half-created, or stub the filesystem state the fast path inspects -- rather
than running N workers and hoping. A race asserted only by repetition is not a reproduction, and the
project's standing rule is that acceptance criteria are verifiable in real time on demand.

Also worth pinning explicitly: verify with BOTH check_mechanism_delta.py --check AND
tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py. This should be a movement of an existing check rather than new
machinery, so it should register no mechanism -- and make lint alone does not cover that test, which
is the gap that sent a sibling change to Gerrit red earlier today.

Context for whoever picks this up: this is NOT a regression introduced by change 2600. Before it
there was no lock at all and workers raced freely; 2600 narrowed the window substantially and this
closes the remainder. The fix is cheap -- an flock on a local file costs microseconds and is taken a
handful of times per run, during collection and therefore off any test's timeout budget.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/e2e/_toolchain.py::provision_toolchain` checks `_satisfied()` BEFORE taking the flock,
and `_satisfied` treats the harness bundle as ready on mere existence
(`(js_dir / BUNDLE_RELPATH).is_file()`). esbuild writes `dist/roundtrip.mjs` in place, so
under `-n 4 --dist worksteal` a worker can see the path exist while the lock holder is still
writing it, return early, and run `node dist/roundtrip.mjs` against a truncated file. The
failure would surface as a confusing harness/JSON error rather than as a provisioning problem.

Raised as an LLM-Review advisory on change 2600 (`tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:151`). It did not
block that change and was deliberately left to land the priority-0 unblocker first; nothing
about it is fixed by what merged.

## Approach

Delete the unlocked fast path and evaluate `_satisfied()` INSIDE the lock. The fast path was
an optimisation for the already-provisioned case, but an `fcntl.flock` on a local file costs
microseconds and is taken a handful of times per run (once per xdist worker at collection,
plus at most once per session in the fixture fallback), so the saving it buys does not pay for
the race it opens. A waiter blocks only while a peer is genuinely provisioning, and it waits
during COLLECTION, which is not on any test timeout budget — the property bug
9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091 established.

## Scope

- `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` — move the `_satisfied()` check inside `_install_lock`.
- `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` — extend the concurrency oracle.

## Testing

The existing two-process concurrency test brackets only the install step. Extend the stub
`npm` to bracket `run build` as well, and assert the whole event sequence across both
processes is disjoint (no span of either step opens while another is open). Pre-fix, a second
process returns as soon as the bundle path appears, so its span closes before the builder
finishes and the sequence interleaves; post-fix it cannot. Verify RED before GREEN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `provision_toolchain` performs no readiness check outside the lock. Checked by the
      extended two-process test, which must fail against the current code and pass after.
- [ ] A caller never returns while a peer is mid-build. Checked by the disjoint-span assertion
      over bracketed install AND build events from both processes.
- [ ] No regression in the existing behaviour. Checked by
      `pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q` and a cold
      `pytest tests/e2e -n 4 --dist worksteal -q` completing with no worker kill.

file_impact.reason: move the _satisfied() readiness check inside _install_lock so no caller can observe a half-written harness bundle through the unlocked fast path
extend the two-process concurrency oracle to bracket the build step as well as the install, and assert both spans are disjoint across processes

compiled_state.title: e2e toolchain provisioning has an unlocked fast path that can expose a half-written harness bundle
